text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 23,810.85, up 1.58% on the day and 4.66% over the last five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.25% (5‑day gain 3.61%). Advances outpaced declines (311 vs 179) and the breadth score sat at 49.6 in a neutral zone, indicating a fairly wide‑ranging rally across large‑cap stocks. The India VIX, a volatility gauge, ticked higher to 15.72 (+1.42%), suggesting modest risk appetite.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding ₹7,284 cr today and a cumulative ₹21,705 cr over five days, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold ₹3,712 cr. Leading sectors were Infrastructure, Capital Markets, Pharma and Oil & Gas, while IT and Financial Services showed weakness. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 1.07 for Nifty, a max‑pain level near 23,800 and an expected range of 23,677‑24,244, with resistance (“call wall”) at 25,000 and support (“put wall”) at 23,000.

Watch the 23,700‑23,800 zone for possible support and the 23,920‑24,000 area for resistance, especially if the Nifty tests the 23,701 pivot (S1). A break above the 24,000‑24,500 range could trigger a move toward the 24,920 resistance, while a slip below 23,500 may invite further selling. Keep an eye on US mid‑term election fallout and crude oil price drops, as they can influence the rupee and commodity‑linked stocks.
